messages:
Alex: FYI p99 token latency spiked in eu-west ~14:20 UTC. p50/p95 stable but p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.5s. tokens/sec for the region stayed flat. anyone seen this pattern before?
Mira: Noted. Was there any recent network deploy or MTU change in eu-west? p99 + flat qps smells like packetization / fragmentation on the hotshard NICs.
Jax: I saw an alert storm in Grafana at the same time — alert rule fired for token-latency-p99 but it was noisy because the query uses avg_over_time on a tail histogram. We should be using histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...)) by (le, route)) instead.
Sam: attaching a quick log slice from one affected host (shortened):
```
2026-03-15T14:20:12Z host=gpu-a1 eu-west1 conn_retries=3 rpc=dispatch latency_ms=1530 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-7b q=quantized
2026-03-15T14:20:12Z host=gpu-a1 kernel_msg=NET_RX_DROP reason=mtu_mismatch if=eth0
```
Mira: that kernel_msg stands out. We rolled a network agent patch at 13:58 that toggles off jumbo frames if driver mismatch. Could be a partial rollback running on a subset of hosts.
sre-bot: ALERT token-latency-p99 eu-west firing (2/3 groups) — linked: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/token-econ-dashboard
Alex: Good catch. If MTU mismatch caused fragmentation, KV cache miss patterns could also amplify per-token latency even without qps increase. Any prometheus queries to correlate?
Jax: Try correlating per-host network errors and per-route p99:
```
sum(rate(node_network_receive_errs_total{region="eu-west"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
vs
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{region="eu-west"}[5m])) by (le, instance, route, model_quant))
```
Li: Also add tokens/sec by model_quant so we can check if quantized vs fp32 diverge:
```
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total{region="eu-west"}[1m])) by (instance, model_quant)
```
Sam: I dug into logs; ~30 hosts saw NET_RX_DROP around 14:20. Most are on a single NIC firmware version. Ops, any idea if we pushed a firmware/driver?
Mira: We did a rolling driver update last night to 2.4.1 but a small batch was on 2.3.9 due to size constraints. Looks like the driver toggles jumbo frame negotiation differently. Partial roll = asymmetric MTU.
Alex: Action items: 1) Ops to isolate the 2.3.9 hosts and revert network agent flags (Mira). 2) Jax to patch the Grafana alert to use histogram_quantile and reduce evaluation window to 5m -> avoid avg smoothing. 3) Li to add tokens/sec by model_quant panel + per-host network error panel to the token-econ dashboard. 4) Sam to collect packet-dump from one host for infra debugging.
Mira: I'll tag the hosts and start the network agent rollback now. ETA 20m.
Jax: I'll open a quick PR for the alert rule, link it here when ready. Suggest replacement rule:
```
- alert: TokenLatencyP99
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, instance)) > 1.0
  for: 2m
```
Li: I'll add the panels and a short note on the dashboard explaining MTU-correlated investigation steps.
Sam: attaching pcap to the ticket once I finish upload.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Once rollback is done let's run a short synthetic against the hotshard and confirm p99 returns to baseline. Also consider adding an automated check in our pre-rolling job to verify MTU uniformity across pool before driver rollouts. :thumbsup:
